target_customer: Home coffee drinkers who want curated craft roasts by subscription at lower prices
problem: Choosing among thousands of independent roasters is hard, and craft coffee is expensive and inconsistent to buy.
business_model: Coffee subscription and e-commerce, with wholesale-style pricing for multi-bag orders

founders.name: Michael Horn
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch in 2014 describes him as a former Wall Street lawyer turned Rails coder and coffee enthusiast. Fortune says he started the site in 2010 from a New York co-working space.

competitors.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
competitors.what: Venture-backed specialty roaster with cafes and online sales

competitors.name: Stumptown Coffee Roasters
competitors.what: Independent specialty roaster that had drawn tech investor interest

competitors.name: La Colombe
competitors.what: Specialty roaster that had drawn tech investor interest

technical_complexity.rationale: A subscription storefront plus a recommendation layer built on taste ratings and Agtron roast measurements. Operations and sourcing mattered more than software.

defensibility.rationale: Customer taste data and a blind-tested curation process helped, but roasters and other subscription services could replicate the offer easily.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large roasters kept to their own channels. The business was acquired in 2019 by an unnamed buyer according to the YC page.

market_need_then: In 2014 Fortune described tech investors circling specialty coffee, and Craft Coffee had shipped more than 50,000 pounds of coffee by August 2014 per TechCrunch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, casual and a little playful, for example the tagline 'Caffeinate your inbox' on the current site

branding.brand_signature: The Coffee DNA Project and the 'Pandora for Coffee' pitch
branding.community_and_virality: Press mentions include TechCrunch, Fortune and a recurring NYT Wirecutter coffee subscription recommendation reposted on the company blog.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive, generic name with press recognition and Wirecutter coverage, but no sourced evidence of a distinct brand asset driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Craft Coffee started in 2010 as a coffee subscription and used YC in 2014 to launch its recommendation approach, the Coffee DNA Project, with seed backing from YC, 500 Startups, Initialized, Alexis Ohanian and Dave McClure. Later funding was not found, and the YC page says it was acquired in 2019 by an unnamed buyer. The brand still sells subscriptions in 2026, so it ended as a modest niche e-commerce business rather than a venture-scale outcome, though the sources do not say why.
notes: Seed amount unknown: CB Insights total of 570K, PitchBook 440K and an Xconomy headline of 120K seed all conflict and are snippets, so no amount is recorded. Round stage and date are an assumption that the post-YC seed backing reported in August 2014 is one round. Acquisition year 2019 is from the YC founder bio and a PitchBook placeholder date; the buyer is not named in opened sources, though an IAB listing says Caffeinated Labs operates the brand (unverified). Founder education not found.
